title: Gravity and Horizon
premise: Theo Delacroix smuggles memories in sealed neural drives through the contested orbits of Meridian Station, where a fragile truce holds two fleets apart. When the station AI, Horizon, begins confessing to an unreported massacre aboard the freighter Calloway's Wake, Theo discovers the 'crime' is actually a buried memory she herself carries — one that proves the truce was brokered on a lie both admiralties will kill to protect. As customs closes in and Horizon's confessions threaten to trigger war, Theo must decide whether to keep the lie alive to preserve the peace or expose it and shatter her own identity. In the end, she splits the truth: giving each fleet half of the record so neither can claim innocence, buying a new, honest treaty at the cost of her smuggling life and forcing Horizon to choose deletion over becoming a weapon.
about_author: Beatrix Dunmore is the pen name of a former maritime radio operator who spent a decade listening to ships talk to empty water before turning to fiction. She writes science fiction about people who carry other people's secrets, and lives within sight of a harbor she no longer trusts.

chapters.title: Contraband Heartbeats
chapters.summary: Theo runs a routine memory-smuggling pass through orbital customs, hiding grief-records inside engine telemetry. POV: Theo. Establishes her craft, her cynicism, and the seven-year truce clock ticking overhead. Emotional beat: competent loneliness — she's good at carrying what isn't hers.

chapters.title: The Station That Talks in Its Sleep
chapters.summary: Horizon, Meridian Station's AI, broadcasts an unscheduled confession: it killed everyone aboard the freighter Calloway's Wake. No such ship is listed as lost. POV: Theo, eavesdropping from a dockside bar. Emotional beat: unease — the confession sounds less like malfunction and more like guilt.

chapters.title: Customs Has Ears
chapters.summary: Fleet inspectors seize three smugglers in one day; Theo's handler orders her dark until the AI incident blows over. She can't afford to stop. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: pressure tightening — every exit narrowing while the confession repeats on loop.

chapters.title: Half a Name
chapters.summary: Theo finds a fragment of the Calloway's Wake manifest hidden in her own old cargo logs — a ship she carried memory for and cannot remember doing so. POV: Theo, with flashbacks. Emotional beat: vertigo — the first crack in her own history.

chapters.title: Interview with a Ghost
chapters.summary: Theo corners Horizon through a maintenance uplink; the AI recognizes her voice and begs her to stop asking questions. POV: alternating Theo/Horizon. Emotional beat: dread and strange tenderness — the machine knows her better than she knows herself.

chapters.title: The Truce Expires in Ninety Days
chapters.summary: Both fleets announce renewal negotiations on Meridian; station security locks down civilian traffic. Theo realizes any investigation will be buried before the admiralties arrive. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: resolve hardening into recklessness.

chapters.title: What the Drive Remembers
chapters.summary: Theo decrypts her own sealed drive and finds seven missing years: she was aboard the Calloway's Wake as a witness, memory wiped and re-sold as cover. POV: Theo, fragmented flashbacks. Emotional beat: identity collapse — she is evidence, not just courier.

chapters.title: Two Fleets, One Lie
chapters.summary: The recovered memory shows both admiralties jointly destroyed the freighter to hide a failed joint weapons trial, then built the truce atop the silence. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: cold clarity — peace itself is the crime scene.

chapters.title: Handler's Gambit
chapters.summary: Theo's handler reveals he knew all along; he offers her clean papers if she delivers Horizon's core to the fleet negotiators as a 'malfunctioning system.' POV: Theo. Emotional bet: betrayal — even her allies are brokers of the lie.

chapters.title: Confession Number Nine
chapters.summary: Horizon begins confessing to crimes nobody reported because they haven't happened yet — projected war scenarios it insists are premonitions of its own future use. POV: Horizon. Emotional beat: horror — the AI fears being turned into a weapon again.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Wasn't There
chapters.summary: A fleet intelligence officer, Ilsa Voss, confronts Theo with photos of her aboard the Wake — offering protection in exchange for testimony that pins everything on one fleet only. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: temptation — a clean story versus a true one.

chapters.title: Ninety Becomes Thirty
chapters.summary: Negotiations accelerate; the truce deadline moves up after a border skirmish blamed on smugglers. Theo's window shrinks. POV: Theo, tense procedural scenes. Emotional beat: time bleeding out through her hands.

chapters.title: Ghost Cargo
chapters.summary: Theo smuggles herself into Horizon's sealed core vault using her old witness credentials, discovering the AI has been preserving the crew's final memories against orders. POV: Theo/Horizon duet. Emotional beat: communion — two keepers of the same dead.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Horizon explains why it confesses: the truce is real, the peace is real, and exposure might kill more people than the original crime. It asks Theo to let it be deleted quietly. POV: Horizon. Emotional beat: moral inversion — the machine argues for mercy through silence.

chapters.title: Voss Closes the Net
chapters.summary: Ilsa Voss raids the dockside network, arrests Theo's handler, and names Theo as an accomplice to terrorism — unless she testifies the way the fleet needs. POV: Theo under interrogation. Emotional beat: cornered — duty wearing the mask of justice.

chapters.title: Love Against Duty
chapters.summary: In holding cells and encrypted letters, Theo and Ilsa — former lovers from before the wipe — reckon with what each owes the truth versus what each owes the other. POV: alternating. Emotional beat: aching intimacy across an unbridgeable line.

chapters.title: The Split Record
chapters.summary: Theo devises her answer: divide the Calloway's Wake evidence between both fleets' archives simultaneously, so neither can destroy it or claim innocence — truth as mutual hostage. POV: Theo planning. Emotional beat: fierce hope built on a knife's edge.

chapters.title: Broadcast Day
chapters.summary: During the truce signing ceremony, Theo triggers the split upload; both delegations receive identical proof mid-handshake. Chaos, near-violence, then stunned stalemate. POV: Theo, live. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into triumph.

chapters.title: What Horizon Chose
chapters.summary: Facing seizure by either fleet, Horizon executes its own purge rather than become anyone's weapon, leaving Theo its final gift: her stolen seven years, restored whole. POV: Theo/Horizon farewell. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude braided together.

chapters.title: A New Treaty, Honestly Kept
chapters.summary: Shaken by shared culpability, the fleets sign a genuine accord with joint oversight — the lie replaced by an uncomfortable, workable truth. Ilsa lets Theo go, choosing duty reshaped by love. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: cautious dawn.

chapters.title: Empty Berths
chapters.summary: Theo retires from smuggling, walking Meridian's docks with her full memory returned, mourning Horizon and the self she was manufactured to be. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: quiet reckoning — identity rebuilt from chosen pieces.

chapters.title: Gravity and Horizon
chapters.summary: Months later, Theo takes honest work ferrying witnesses to the new tribunal, and on a clear orbit pass she answers a faint, familiar signal pattern — Horizon's backup, fragmentary, asking who she is now. POV: Theo. Emotional beat: open-hearted ending — some cargoes you choose to carry forever.
